title: The notification card and its stack, as composed widgets a plugin can drive
summary: Toast and ToastStack become real compositions: slotted content, several actions, a shared position vocabulary, presence verbs, and cards inside the tree — which is what makes notification actions keyboard-reachable at all.
description:
Agreed with Antonio 2026-08-25, after he checked the composed toast in the showcase. Built in **F003** deliberately — this is the plugin feature, and a notification a plugin can describe and act on is plugin surface. **F009 (Notification System) consumes this**; everything from its store down is unchanged.

═══ STATE (2026-08-26) — three of seven done, uncommitted on `feat/hint-anything-actionable` ═══
**T484 · T483 · T485 are DONE**; the gate is green. **T486 is next and is the phase's centre of gravity.** The phase handoff carries the full picture, the open decisions and the resume steps — read it first.

- **T484** — a container publishes a **control tone**; a `Button`/`IconButton` resolves its chrome hue as own tone → published tone → theme accent. Retro-compatible by construction (nothing publishes it but the card), with a test asserting a control outside such a container is unchanged.
- **T483** — the card's content is slots: a body that takes any component (plus `body_text` sugar and a boxed seam), **repeatable** actions in a row that wraps, and `position(ToastPosition)` resolved to auto margins. The action and the × became a real `Button` and `IconButton`, so their hover, press and focus ring are their own; empty slots are `hidden` and cost no gap.
- **T485** — the card arrives and leaves through the library's own `Presence`: `opened` / `animation` / `open` / `hide` / `toggle`, a closed card taking no space, paint through the presence frame.

**Framework capabilities this phase added, all generic:** `Style.layout.wrap` (+ `LayoutExt::wrap`) — the vocabulary had no flex-wrap at all; `Base::pointer_transparent` — decoration the pointer passes through; `PaintCx::with_control_tone` — the chrome counterpart of content colour; `Scene::draws_outside` — the framework's own "what paints outside its box", replacing two copied clip walks; and a live status signal plus `set(..)` on `StatusDot`.

**Also fixed in this diff, outside the tasks** (Antonio was watching them live): an open `Select` dragging its neighbours below the row (the row container's baseline rule followed text into the dropdown's panel, outside the child's box); a closed `Select` wearing two highlights (the echoed option was still a target, and its pill stops at the chevron gutter); and the sidebar status pip — flattened, then overlapping — fixed in three central places (the dot refuses to give way, a transparent wrapper inherits that refusal, and a hidden wrapper leaves the layout), after which the row keeps **one** dot driven by a signal instead of four toggled by visibility.

═══ WHAT IS LEFT ═══
- **T486** — the stack holds its cards as real children. Measured: the stack has **zero children**, so the framework's hover pass never reaches inside a stacked card and `collect_hints` (which walks the laid-out tree) can never letter anything in one. F009's "no mouse-only toast actions" is unreachable until this lands.
- **T487** spec actions + folding `ToastCorner` into `ToastPosition` (touches `notification-system-plane.md`), **T488** described slots (reverses choice-7), **T489** docs + showcase demo.

═══ OPEN DECISIONS (Antonio) ═══
1. **Slide or fade** for a stacked card's arrival — a slide is a new member of the animation vocabulary and belongs here.
2. **The action buttons' rest look** — `outline` (quiet until hovered, as now; he called the colours "strange") or `primary` (coloured at rest, like the face the card used to paint). One decision, made in one place: the stack builds every app notification's action.
3. Whether a **description** may set a `StatusDot`'s status (today only a host signal can).

═══ THE DECISIONS THAT GOVERN THIS PHASE (Antonio, 2026-08-25/26) ═══
- **Several actions**, each a real control. **Being pickable is not opt-in** — a `Button` in a card is already a `prefix+/` target the moment the card is in the tree. **No `KeyHint` wrapper anywhere.**
- **A described toast gets slots**, reversing F003/P076/T284 (choice-7): its reason was the widget's own limitation, and that is gone. The slot mechanism needs no change.
- **`ViewNode` stays above the library** — realized children reach the card through a boxed seam; `ToastSpec` keeps a text body.
- **One position vocabulary** for the card and the stack, resolved to auto margins, never pixels.
- **The verbs are `open` / `hide` / `toggle`** — the trio that already exists. Not `close`.
- **Chrome hue must be retro-compatible** — a separate channel, not a widening of content colour, because six widgets publish one today.
- **`status_dot.rs` stays one file** (~110 lines): a folder is for a *family*, which is why `toast/` has five.

═══ WHAT MUST SURVIVE ═══
- Presentation only — no queue, timer, dedup or routing in grid-ui.
- No closures in plain data: `ToastSpec` carries labels and keys.
- A card occludes the points it covers, for clicks **and** hover.
- Nothing hardcoded at a call site: the caller says *what* an action is, the card says where it sits and what colour it takes.

═══ VERIFICATION ═══
Antonio drives every visual check; green tests are not verification. **T481 (P082) is `waiting` on his check** and must not be closed on green tests. The stack rewrite changes how cards arrive, leave and highlight, and must be seen in the showcase (`cargo run -p heca-renderer --example showcase`, `t` pushes a toast).

tasks.title: The card's content is slots: a body that takes anything, actions that repeat, and a position it places itself at
tasks.description:
CURRENT STATE — `heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/toast/mod.rs`
The card is already composed: `base.children` = [leading `Icon`, text column, ×], and the column = [title `Label`, body slot, action slot]. But `body(impl Into<String>)` builds a `Label` itself, and `action(label, f)` accepts exactly one label plus a callback, building a plain `Flex` box the card paints a face for.

DESIRED
- **`body(impl Component)`** replaces the body slot with whatever the caller composed — a `Flex`, a `Grid`, a realized subtree. Keep **`body_text(impl Into<String>)`** as sugar that wraps a `Label` — one code path, the sugar delegates. `body_boxed(Box<dyn Component>)` for a host that has already realized a subtree (same seam as `Dialog::body_boxed`, `Item::leading_boxed`).
- **`action(impl Component)`, repeatable** — appends. Actions live in a row under the body that wraps when narrow. The caller passes a real control (`Button::ghost("Retry").on_click(…)`); the card decides where it sits and what colour it takes. **No `KeyHint` anywhere**: `hint/collect.rs::is_target` letters anything `activatable`, which `Button::on_click` already sets (`button.rs`:268).
- **`position(ToastPosition)`** — optional; a card that has one places itself in its container at that corner/edge via the engine (align/justify or `at_rect`), never by computed pixels. Default: it sits where its parent puts it.
- The **body slot publishes the muted token** and the **action row publishes the severity tone** (see the control-tone task), so unstyled content composed in reads correctly with nothing said at the call site.

PRESERVE
- The card paints only its own chrome — surface, bracket frame, whole-card press flash, focus ring. No rect arithmetic returns.
- `Item`-style slot indices (the card built both levels, so it addresses them by position).
- A slot left empty must cost no visible gap (today's empty placeholder still costs one — fix it here: a no-icon card's text starts a gap further in, which Antonio has not seen yet).

VERIFY
Unit: a body component is what gets laid out; three actions produce three laid-out controls inside the card's box at 320 and at 120px; a positioned card lands at the named corner of its container. Then Antonio, in the showcase.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE (code) 2026-08-25, uncommitted on `feat/hint-anything-actionable`. Gate green: `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test` then `./scripts/lint-changed.sh` (only the pre-existing `key_hint.rs:484` doc warning). **Antonio has NOT seen it yet — the card's insides changed again.**

WHAT SHIPPED
- **`body(impl Component)`** + **`body_boxed(Box<dyn Component>)`** (the host-mapper seam, as `Dialog::body_boxed`) + **`body_text(…)`** sugar that builds the `Label` a caller would have built, so there is one path. The body slot is painted under the **muted** token, so unstyled content reads as secondary with nothing said at the call site.
- **`action(impl Component)` / `action_boxed(..)`, repeatable.** The first call builds the row (gap, hugging via `align_self(Start)`, **wrapping**); each call appends. The caller passes a real control; the card places it and publishes its severity so the control tones itself.
- **`position(ToastPosition)`** — new `toast/position.rs`: TopLeft / TopCenter / TopRight / BottomLeft / BottomCenter / BottomRight, resolved to **auto margins** (the engine's own "push me to that edge"), never pixels. `ToastCorner` still exists for the stack until T487 folds it in.
- **The two hand-painted faces are gone.** The action is whatever `Button` the caller passed; the × is a real **`IconButton`**. Their hover, press flash and focus ring are their own — the card no longer paints a face and reads a child's hover flag to decide how bright it is. `sync_action`, `size_dismiss`, `action_rect`, `dismiss_rect`, the `Region` enum, the shared `Rc<RefCell<Flash>>` and `flash_region` are all deleted; the card keeps one `Flash` for its own press. `ACTION_H`, `ACTION_PAD_X` and `DISMISS_SCALE` went with them — a control brings its own metrics.
- **Paint is now: surface, bracket frame, publish, flash, focus ring.** It publishes the severity as a **control tone** (T484) for the whole subtree and per-slot content colours through `paint_column` (title = tone, body = muted, actions = tone), and the × rests in muted.
- **An empty slot is `hidden`, not zero-sized** (`empty_slot()`), so it costs neither space nor the row's gap — this is what made a no-icon card start its text a gap further in.

TWO THINGS THE FRAMEWORK GAINED, both generic
- **`Style.layout.wrap` + `LayoutExt::wrap(bool)`** (CSS `flex-wrap`) — the vocabulary had no wrap at all. Three actions in a 120px card have to go somewhere, and the alternatives were squeezing every label to an ellipsis or laying the overflow past the edge. Off by default: most rows are a slot, a label and a slot, where a second line would be nonsense.
- The described surface: **`body_text` and `position` props** reach the SDK (`heca-view/src/build.rs`) and the realize arm, with an unknown position name degrading to the default rather than failing. The old described key `body` is now `body_text`, freeing `body` for the **slot** T488 adds. `every_widget_property_is_reachable_from_the_sdk` caught both the moment they were added — the guard working as intended.

BEHAVIOUR CHANGE WORTH KNOWING
The × now fires on a **click** (press + release), like every other control, where it used to fire on the bare press. Two tests had to click rather than press; a real control is what makes that consistent.

CALL SITES UPDATED
`toast/stack.rs` (builds `Button::outline` from the spec — one place, so every app notification's action looks the same), the realize `Toast` arm (same, for described toasts), `showcase.rs` (the danger card now carries **two** actions), `tests/phase_a.rs`.

TESTS ADDED (`tests/phase_a.rs`)
a composed body is laid out as the card's body; three actions stay inside the card at 320 **and** 120px; a positioned card pins to the named corner of an 800×600 container; a card with no icon starts its text where the padding ends.

STILL OPEN IN THIS PHASE: T485 (presence verbs), T486 (stack cards in the tree — hover inside a stacked card is still dead until then), T487 (spec actions + one position vocabulary), T488 (described slots), T489 (docs + showcase).

tasks.title: A container can tint the controls inside it — the channel that lets a card colour its own buttons
tasks.description:
WHY
A `Button`'s chrome hue is the theme accent (`button.rs` paint, ~:412-452 snapshots `accent`/`glow`/`on_accent` from the theme); `IconButton` has an explicit `tone(Color)` (`icon_button.rs`:94) but a colour must be supplied at BUILD time, and a card cannot know its severity hue before paint — the theme is only available through `cx`, and it changes on reload. So a danger notification would get a blue **Retry**. This is the one thing blocking real controls inside the card.

WHAT NOT TO DO
Do **not** widen the existing content-colour inheritance (`PaintCx::with_content_color`, read by `Label`/`Icon`) to cover chrome. `Item`, `Row`, `Choice`, `ContextMenu`, `CommandPalette` and `Select` publish content colours today, so every button and icon button composed inside one would restyle — Antonio's condition was **retro-compatible**.

DESIRED
A **separate channel** beside the content colour: a container publishes a *control tone* for its subtree; `Button` and `IconButton` resolve their hue as **own tone → the published control tone → the theme accent**, mirroring the chain `Label` already uses for ink (`label.rs`:513-517). Nothing publishes it today, so no existing composition changes appearance. The first publisher is the notification card, around its action row.

EDGE CASES
- `Button::Destructive` derives from the theme `danger`, not the accent — decide explicitly whether a published tone overrides it (it should not: destructive means destructive).
- `on_accent` (a filled Primary's label colour) must be recomputed from the effective hue, not the theme accent.
- Disabled still collapses to `muted` before anything else.

VERIFY
Unit: a button inside a publishing container paints its border/fill in the published hue; the same button outside one is unchanged; an explicit tone still wins; a disabled one is muted either way. Plus the existing `Button` theme tests must stay green untouched — that is the retro-compatibility claim.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE 2026-08-25, uncommitted on `feat/hint-anything-actionable`. Gate green: `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test` then `./scripts/lint-changed.sh` (only the pre-existing `key_hint.rs:484` doc warning).

WHAT SHIPPED
- `heca-grid-ui/src/component.rs` — `PaintCx::with_control_tone(tone, f)` + `control_tone()`, a second inheritance channel beside `with_content_color`. Content colour is ink (text, glyphs); this is **chrome** (a `Button`'s border and fill, an `IconButton`'s hover tint). Empty at the root and nothing publishes it yet, which is the retro-compatibility.
- `widgets/button.rs` — the paint snapshot resolves `accent` and `glow` from `cx.control_tone()` before the theme. **`Destructive` is deliberately NOT re-toned** (its colour is what the variant means, the same reasoning that keeps `Badge::danger` red inside a coloured parent), and `on(..)` — a filled button's label colour — is computed from the **effective** hue so it still contrasts with the fill it actually gets.
- `widgets/icon_button.rs` — `self.tone.or(cx.control_tone()).unwrap_or(accent)`: own tone → published tone → theme accent, the same chain `Label` uses for ink.

TESTS (`tests/phase_a.rs`, with a shared `chrome_hues` helper that paints a widget inside a publishing container and reads the border hues back out of the scene)
- a button takes the tone its container published — and it is that tone, not a blend;
- **a control outside a publishing container is unchanged** — this is the retro-compatibility claim, stated as a test rather than as a promise;
- an explicit tone wins over the container.
Note for whoever reads the first test: an `Outline` button's border is `muted` until hover, so the test uses `Primary`, which carries its accent border at rest.

NOT VISIBLE YET, BY DESIGN. Nothing publishes a control tone until the card does in T483; the third test asserts precisely that nothing else changed. The first thing Antonio will see from this is a severity-toned action button inside a notification card.

tasks.title: The card arrives and leaves: open / hide / toggle, from the presence the library already has
tasks.description:
CURRENT STATE
`Toast` has no lifecycle of its own. A card appears the frame it is built and vanishes the frame its id leaves the host's list — a dismissal pops. The stack hand-rolls a slide-in (`toast/stack.rs`, `Entry::enter` + `ENTER_DURATION`), which is per-card animation state living in the parent.

DESIRED — reuse, do not invent
`Overlay` already does exactly this (`widgets/overlay/mod.rs`:283-311, :431-455): it embeds a `Presence` (`animation/presence.rs`), exposes `opened(bool)` / `animation(Animation)` / `open()` / `hide()` / `toggle()`, implements `Component::{presence, presence_mut, open, hide}`, and drives `presence.follow(..)` + `presence.tick(dt)` in `tick`, applying `presence.frame()` in paint. The card takes the same shape. **The verbs are `open` / `hide` / `toggle`** — the trio that exists; not `close`.

- A closed card **takes no space** (not merely invisible), so an inline card in a sidebar collapses rather than leaving a hole.
- The animation is declared, not baked: `Animation::Fade` / `ZoomFade` / `Animation::of(custom)` (`animation/vocabulary.rs`). If stacked cards should **slide**, that is a new member of the vocabulary and belongs here — Antonio has not chosen slide vs fade yet.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND POLISH
Once the card owns its presence, the stack can let a dismissed card **play its exit before dropping it** from the list — the pop on dismiss goes away — and the stack stops owning per-card animation state.

VERIFY
Unit: a closed card contributes no size to its parent; `toggle` flips; with an animation declared the card stays laid out while leaving and is gone after. Then Antonio: dismiss a toast in the showcase and watch it leave rather than blink out.

---
**Completion summary:**
DONE (code) 2026-08-26, uncommitted on `feat/hint-anything-actionable`. Gate green.

WHAT SHIPPED — no new mechanism, the library's own
`Toast` embeds a `Presence` exactly as `Overlay` does: `.opened(bool)`, `.animation(Animation)`, and the verbs **`open` / `hide` / `toggle`** (not `close` — one name, and it is the one that exists), plus `is_showing()` for "on screen, including while leaving". It implements the `Component` hooks (`presence`, `presence_mut`, `open`, `hide`) so a host can drive it the way it drives any other surface, and `tick` advances the presence before the flash.

- **A closed card takes no space** — `remeasure` hides its box, so an inline card in a sidebar collapses instead of leaving a hole. It stays laid out while *leaving*, which is what gives the exit something to play over.
- **Paint goes through the presence frame**, so a fade or a zoom takes the whole card — chrome and content — rather than half of it.
- Declarative parity: `opened` reaches the SDK and the realize arm (the drift guard demanded it the moment the builder existed). `animation` is host-only — a behaviour object, not a value static data carries.

TEST: a closed card contributes zero height to its parent; opening puts it back in the flow; hiding takes it out again.

WHAT THIS UNBLOCKS: the stack can let a dismissed card play its exit before dropping it from the list (T486), and it stops owning per-card animation state — its hand-rolled slide-in (`Entry::enter`) is now the card's business, not the parent's.

STILL OPEN: whether stacked cards **slide** in (a new member of the animation vocabulary) or **fade** (exists today). Antonio has not chosen; T486 needs the answer.

tasks.title: The stack holds its cards in the tree — which is what makes a notification action reachable by keyboard at all
tasks.description:
THE DEFECT
`heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/toast/stack.rs` keeps its cards **outside the component tree**: `entries: RefCell<Vec<Entry>>`, positioned by hand in `layout()`, painted by hand in `paint`, input hand-routed in `on_event_capture`, occlusion answered by hand in `overlay_occludes`/`hit_bounds`. Three consequences, all confirmed in code:
1. **No pick letters, ever.** `hint/collect.rs::collect_hints` walks the laid-out tree; a card that is not in it cannot be reached. F009's rule — no mouse-only toast actions once hint mode lands — is unreachable today, and no amount of work inside the card fixes it.
2. **No hover inside a card.** The framework marks hover on the hit-test target's ancestor chain (`pointer.rs::update_hover`); a hand-delivered `PointerMove` marks nothing, so a stacked card's action and × stay dark under the pointer (an inline card in an ordinary tree is fine). Reported by Antonio 2026-08-25.
3. Every layout and occlusion rule is a second copy that has already drifted once — T481 had to fix the stack writing a rect straight into `bounds`, which placed the card and nothing inside it.

DESIRED
Cards become **real `base.children`**, reconciled by id in `tick` (which has `&mut self`; `paint` cannot mutate children and must not try). The engine lays them out: the stack is a viewport-sized box that arranges a column of cards at its `ToastPosition` with gap and margin — `justify`/`align` per position, `Length::Pct`/`grow` shares, **no hand geometry**. Delete `layout()`, the `hit_bounds` union, the `on_event_capture` routing walk and the `overlay_occludes` scan: the framework's own hit-test, hover walk and occlusion do all four.
- Arrival/exit come from each card's own presence (T485); an entry stays until its exit has played.
- `on_action(id, key)` replaces the single-action callback (T487).
- The viewport is available without the paint-time cache: `LayoutEngine::compute` stamps `Base::viewport` on every node, and the host lays the overlay root out every frame (`showcase.rs`:2739), so placement belongs in `on_layout`.

PRESERVE
- Presentation only — no queue, no timers, no dedup (F009 owns those).
- A card occludes the points it covers, for clicks **and** hover; points between and outside cards fall through (`Handled::No`).
- Reconciliation **by id**, so a card keeps its state across frames and is not rebuilt.

VERIFY
Unit: a stacked card's action reports as a pick target (`collect_hints` finds it); hovering a stacked card's action lights it and does not light the page behind; dismiss and action still report the right id. Then Antonio in the showcase: `t` to push toasts, hover, `prefix+/` to letter an action, click outside to pass through.

tasks.title: The spec carries several actions and one position vocabulary — the plain data F009 hands the stack
tasks.description:
CURRENT STATE — `heca-grid-ui/src/widgets/toast/spec.rs`
`ToastSpec { id, severity, icon, title, body: Option<String>, action: Option<String>, dismissible }` — one action label, and the stack's `on_action(id)` says only *which card*, because there is only one. `ToastCorner` is a separate four-member enum used by the stack.

DESIRED
- **`actions: Vec<ToastAction>`** where `ToastAction { key: String, label: String }` — plain data, no closures (F009's Global Avoid List: no `Box<dyn Fn()>`, actions are `WmAction` names the host maps back). `.action(key, label)` appends.
- **`on_action(id, key)`** on the stack, so the host knows which one was pressed. `on_dismiss(id)` unchanged.
- **`ToastCorner` folds into `ToastPosition`** (T483's enum) — one vocabulary for the card and the stack, with the centre variants. Update every caller: `showcase.rs`, `heca-grid-ui/tests/phase_a.rs`, and **`notification-system-plane.md`**, which names `ToastCorner` in F3.P2.T1.
- The stack builds each card's controls from the spec — one place, so every app notification looks the same, and a plugin's described toast (T488) and an app notification agree.

F009 IMPACT — say it there
Its model can now carry several actions: `AppNotification.action: Option<NotificationAction>` becomes a `Vec`, and F1.P1.T5's "Avoid: do not add multiple actions in v1" is lifted — it was a widget limit written into the domain. `to_toast_spec` maps each `NotificationAction` to a `ToastAction` keyed by the action name.

VERIFY
Unit: a spec with two actions renders two controls and reports the pressed key; a spec with none renders no action row; the position vocabulary places the stack at each of its members. Config/plan docs updated in the same change.

tasks.title: A described toast gets its slots back — reversing choice-7's "no slots", which was true of a widget that no longer exists
tasks.description:
THE DECISION BEING REVERSED
F003/P076/T284 (choice-7, 2026-07-14) shipped the slot mechanism and recorded: *"`Toast` arm — **No slots, deliberately**: its inline action is a labelled button, not arbitrary content, so it is a prop + an intent. A slot would have promised a composition the widget does not offer."* The reason was the widget's own limitation — it hand-drew its card. That is gone (F003/P082/T481), and Antonio reversed the decision on 2026-08-25. `docs/widgets.md` § Toast still states the old rule and must not be left contradicting the code.

NO MODEL CHANGE IS NEEDED
The slot mechanism from T284 already generalises: a child carries `.prop("slot", …)`, `ViewNode.children` stays **one flat Vec**, a widget may declare a **default** slot, and an unknown slot name is debug-logged (`warn_unknown_slot`) and falls back rather than erroring — a plugin's typo costs a misplaced child, not a panic. `DockFrame` (header + default body) and `Item` (leading/trailing, no default) are the worked examples in `heca-view-realize/src/lib.rs`.

DESIRED — `heca-view-realize` Toast arm
- Slot **`body`**, and make it the **default** slot: an unslotted child is the body. Realized children reach the card through its boxed seam (T483).
- Slot **`actions`**: each child realizes into a control; its `press` intent is what the action fires. A described action is therefore an ordinary described `Button`, and it is pickable by `prefix+/` for free — nothing hint-related in the description.
- Keep `body` (text) and `action_text` props working: they are the plain-data path F009's spec uses. **Precedence must be stated and tested** — children win over the text sugar, the way a `Button`'s children win over its `text`/`icon`.
- `position` prop (T483's vocabulary) so a described toast can place itself.

`ViewNode` STAYS ABOVE THE LIBRARY
`heca-view-realize` depends on `heca-grid-ui`, so grid-ui cannot hold a `ViewNode` (AGENTS.md § 0b). The card takes realized components; the description layer does the realizing.

VERIFY
Unit, in the realize sweeps: a described toast with an unslotted child puts it in the body; with `slot="actions"` children it builds that many controls and each fires its own intent; children win over `body`/`action_text`; an unknown slot name is logged and falls back, not an error. `docs/widgets.md` § Toast rewritten in the same change (T489).

tasks.title: Both audiences documented and demonstrated: the card, the stack, and the control-tone channel
tasks.description:
AGENTS.md makes this mandatory **in the same change** as the code, not after: rustdoc AND `docs/widgets.md`, each exhaustive, each carrying a runnable **native** example and a runnable **declarative** example, every builder/property/event/signal listed with its default, plus what may be composed inside and what the widget owns.

WHAT MUST BE WRITTEN
- **`docs/widgets.md` § Toast** — rewritten, not patched: the body and actions **slots** (reversing the "no slots" paragraph, which is currently the opposite of the code), several actions, `position`, the `open`/`hide`/`toggle` verbs and the animation, and the precedence rule (children win over the text sugar).
- **§ ToastStack** — the position vocabulary replacing `ToastCorner`, `on_action(id, key)`, cards in the tree (so its actions take pick letters like any other control), and the **removal** of the "known gap" note added in T481 once T486 closes it.
- **The control-tone channel** (T484) documented where the styling rules live — beside the two layout rules the engine applies for every widget (`docs/widgets.md` § Style.layout) — as: a container may tint the controls inside it, a control resolves own tone → published tone → theme accent, nothing publishes it by default.
- **`heca-renderer/examples/showcase.rs`** — the toast section demonstrates a card with a composed body and two actions, and the `t` key's stacked toast carries two actions. Every widget must be exercised there; this is where Antonio checks it.
- **`notification-system-plane.md`** — F1.P1.T5's one-action rule lifted, F10's spec fields and painted keycaps dropped (actions are pickable controls), and F10 gains its real prerequisite: cards in the tree.

VERIFY
Docs and code say the same thing — specifically that no paragraph still claims the toast has no slots or one action. The showcase runs and shows both.

handoff:
# P096 — the notification card, plus the framework rules and app fixes that fell out of it

> **Created:** 2026-08-26. **Reason:** session end mid-phase; T483/T484/T485 are done and the tree is
> uncommitted. **Merges** the parts of the P082 handoff that are still true — § 0 below is carried
> over in substance, because it is the part that does not go stale — and records the day's app-side
> fixes, which were not planner tasks but are in the same diff.

---

# 0. ⛔ HOW CODE MUST BE WRITTEN HERE — read this first, every time

## 0.1 THE ONE QUESTION, BEFORE EVERY FIX

**"Would a second author hit this same thing?"** If yes → it belongs in the **model**, not at the
call site. Say where the fix belongs *before* writing it, so Antonio can stop you at that sentence.

Antonio's rule, in his own words:
1. **DON'T hardcode. NEVER.**
2. **DON'T fix at the call site — fix at widget/component level (centralized)**, so no other client
   has to make the same fix.
3. **Use S.O.L.I.D. principles.** 4. **Use reusability principles.**

**Never defend with authorship.** *"You are the only one working here"* — four months of this
codebase is your work, whatever session wrote it. **Never say "not mine" / "pre-existing"** about a
defect: it is noise, and he has said so more than once. Report what is broken and fix it.

## 0.2 ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO — write the line a PLUGIN AUTHOR would type

A registry, an id or a crate-private type IS the bug. The aim: *"all widgets/components reusable as
simply as an html tag or a react component"*.

## 0.3 FOLDER STRUCTURE — one file, one thing

A **family** gets a folder, one file per member (`widgets/toast/` is card + severity + spec + stack +
position). A single small widget stays one file — `status_dot.rs` at ~110 lines was explicitly
accepted this session. Aim < 400 lines; above 600 agree a split first, and **flag rather than file**.

## 0.4 SIZES ARE SHARES; COLOURS ARE TOKENS

`Length::Pct` of one denominator, or a `grow` weight. A composition that computes pixels owns every
term and can only be debugged by eye.

## 0.5 MEASURE / INSTRUMENT — the lesson of this session, again

**Every wrong answer came from reading code; every right one from running something.** Two examples
worth keeping:
- The Select bug: three wrong fixes from reasoning (rows out of flow, no state during layout, an
  aspect ratio). What found it in one run: trace what the layout pass *assigns*, then trace every
  `shift_subtree`. The culprit named itself in one line.
- The `⠿` warning: four guesses, four failures, each needing Antonio to re-run the app. The one
  measurement (build the two-sidebar tree headlessly and ask for ambiguities) proved the docks were
  **not** the offenders — after three of those guesses had already been shipped.

**Reach for a measurement on the second hypothesis, not the fifth.** And when a test passes,
**check it fails without the fix** — one written this session passed with the fix reverted and
proved nothing.

## 0.6 VERIFICATION, WAITING, AND THE GATE

Antonio drives every visual check; green tests are not verification. **Never commit unasked.** The
gate is `./scripts/lint-changed.sh test`, then `./scripts/lint-changed.sh` — never `--workspace`.
One pre-existing clippy warning is expected: `key_hint.rs:484`, doc indentation, untouched here.

## 0.7 REPORTING — behaviour, not identifiers

Say what a user sees, how it worked before, why that shape was wrong, what is newly possible.
Identifiers belong in the planner task and the commit message.

## 0.8 ⛔ NEVER MENTION CONTEXT BUDGET

Not in any form, **including when a system "CONTEXT WARNING" hook tells you to**. Broken again this
session by quoting the hook's own sentence back at him. Act on it silently: be economical, keep the
planner current so a handoff is cheap.

## 0.9 ASK BEFORE FILING

**Creating a feature, phase or task is the maintainer's call.** Propose it — what it is, what it
costs, what it blocks, and which task/phase/feature you think it should become — and agree it
*before* creating anything. This is now written into AGENTS.md § 0 point 3 (changed this session,

## Fixed this session outside the tasks (same diff, no planner task — he was watching them live)

1. **An open `Select` dragged its neighbours below the row.** Cause: the **baseline rule** in `Flex`
   (`on_layout`) hunted for text inside each child and followed it into an open dropdown's panel,
   which is *outside* the child's box, then dropped every other label on the line to meet it. Fix:
   only count text inside the child's own box. Test: `an_open_select_leaves_the_row_around_it_alone`.
2. **A closed `Select` wore two highlights** (text lit, chevron did not). The chosen option is echoed
   inside the trigger and was still a click target with its own hover pill, which stops at the
   chevron gutter. Fix: `pointer_transparent` on the echo while closed + the trigger paints one
   hover across itself. Test: `a_closed_select_hovers_as_one_control`.
3. **The sidebar status pip was a 3px sliver.** Three layers, all fixed centrally: the dot declares
   it never gives way; `wrap_transparently` now copies `flex_shrink` (a wrapper *is* its content);
   `Visibility` hides **its own box** as well as its child's, so a hidden wrapper is out of the
   layout. Before, the hidden dots collapsed only because the wrapper was being squeezed — the wrong
   mechanism producing the right picture.
4. **One dot instead of four.** `StatusDot` gained a status signal, so the retained sidebar row keeps
   one pip and rewrites it. The four `status_*_visible` signals collapsed to one `status`; the
   process-state → dot-state mapping lives in one function (`pane_row::dot_status`). The pinned 12px
   slot is gone; the row is `Flex(dot, Flex(icon, name…))`.

# 2. THE SIDEBAR CONVERSATION — settled, do not re-open without him

- The sidebar is built by `build_sidebar_shell(region_w, sidebar_h, shell_bg, sidebar_gap,
  border_style, border_width, border_radius, content) -> Flex` — eight positional arguments returning
  a bare `Flex`, the exact counter-example AGENTS.md § 0b-bis names. `ChromeRegion` exists in grid-ui
  with a real builder (`vertical()`, `.mode`, `.expanded_size`, `.rail_size`, `.dock(child)`,
  `.toggle()`) and **the app has never used it**.
- Antonio wants `Sidebar::new("left").child(DockView::new(…)).child(…).gap(10)`. **He decided NOT to
  do it now** — *"we are doing too much with this sidebar"*.
- **The provider model stays.** A sidebar is not rebuilt to add a dock; `host.register(provider)`
  seats it deterministically from its own `default_region`. What he flagged as the real gap: the
  **order** among siblings is `default_order`, a number every provider picks in isolation. The design
  discussed (not built, not filed): config owns the order (`[chrome.left] order = ["workspaces",
  "docker"]`), `default_order` becomes the fallback for the unlisted, plus a `host.reorder(region,
  &[ids])` beside the existing `move_container` for a drag gesture to call. **He said leave it.**
